lead.hed: USS Howard drilled its small-caliber guns in the Northern Pacific
lead.insight: A Navy photograph posted Friday morning shows Chief Gunner's Mate Dalton Daniel explaining an M240 machine gun to the small-caliber action team on the starboard bridge wing of the Arleigh Burke-class guided-missile destroyer USS Howard (DDG 83). The caption says the ship was operating in the Northern Pacific on Oct. 14. Howard is forward-deployed with Destroyer Squadron 15, the Navy's largest destroyer squadron and 7th Fleet's principal surface force. The photograph was taken Oct. 13 by Mass Communication Specialist 1st Class Matt Riggs.

political.hed: Heritage says the Trump-Xi summit bought time and kept leverage
political.insight: Friday's Heritage report on the Sept. 23–25 Washington summit says a prior Heritage analysis expected tactical agreements, not a transformative breakthrough. The published outcomes, the report says, bought time and preserved leverage.

political.hed: A House hearing found union leaders spending dues on their own priorities
political.insight: Thursday's Heritage commentary says a House hearing last month exposed eight years of industrial unions spending members' money on union leaders' personal priorities rather than on members. Political donations were the first finding. The piece says that record should change how Washington hears union leaders when they claim to speak for workers.

tech.hed: Lockheed is putting $300 million into its Grand Prairie missile plant
tech.insight: Defense News reports that Lockheed Martin is investing $300 million to expand its Grand Prairie, Texas, plant, which supports every program in its Missiles and Fire Control business, including PAC-3 MSE, THAAD, the Precision Strike Missile, and the AIM-260. The company said Oct. 14 that the work will help the plant reach record production and feed final assembly in Camden, Arkansas, and Troy, Alabama. The expansion adds 100,000 square feet and converts 85,000 square feet of office space to factory floor, taking the plant past 735,000 square feet.

tech.hed: An Australian firm will let Boxer crews direct drones by voice
tech.insight: Defense News reports that Sydney-based Breaker Industries is working with Rheinmetall Defence Australia on Avalon, a human-machine interface meant to let a Boxer commander direct unmanned systems in the air and on the ground. The firms signed a teaming agreement Oct. 6 at the Land Forces exhibition in Perth. Work continues for twelve months, with trials slated for mid-2027.

culture.hed: A dating standard worth keeping is a man who does not watch porn
culture.insight: Friday's First Things essay says some conservative young men call women's dating standards unrealistic, and that viral checklists about height and income give that complaint a foothold. The writer draws a line: character standards still matter, and refusing a partner who watches pornography is one of them. Some conservatives, the essay says, treat that refusal as unrealistic and dismiss it as feminist.

watch.hed: U.S. soldiers are back in the Panamanian jungle, more than 20 years after the bases changed hands
watch.note: Defense News, Friday: a reinvigorated jungle school is one piece of a growing U.S. military presence in Panama as Washington turns toward the Western Hemisphere. A Sept. 26 medical mission in Metiti included a Joint Task Force-Bravo veterinary technician. More than 20 years after the United States turned its bases over, the partnership is what a renewed hemispheric focus looks like on the ground.
